# Compare two holiday cities with Qwen Chat — step by step

**Hook:**
Imagine typing two city names and, in seconds, getting a clear, easy-to-read comparison of weather, costs, things to do and local vibes. That’s what Qwen Chat can do for you. No travel blogs, no ads — just the facts you need to decide where to go next.

## Before you start
- A free Qwen Chat account (sign-up takes 2 minutes at [qwen.chat](https://qwen.chat))
- Any device with a web browser (phone, tablet or computer)
- About 10 minutes total time

---

## Step 1 — Open Qwen Chat and start a fresh chat
Open your browser and go to [qwen.chat](https://qwen.chat). You’ll see a clean white page with a big message box at the bottom. If the page looks different on your phone, look for a button like “Start chatting” or a plus sign (+) in the corner.
You’ll know it worked when you see the prompt box ready for typing.

💬 Example:
Just open the site — no login needed if you want to try it quickly.

---

## Step 2 — Type your travel request in plain English
In the message box, type a clear sentence that names the two cities and what you want to compare. Keep it simple so the AI understands. If the box isn’t there, tap the plus sign (+) or look for a button like “New chat.”
After you hit send, you’ll see the AI start typing right away.
You’ll know it worked when you see the AI’s first reply beginning with something like “Here’s a quick comparison between…”

💬 Example:
Compare Sydney and Melbourne for a 5-day holiday in October, focusing on weather, cost and things to do.

---

## Step 3 — Read the first quick summary
The AI will give you a short paragraph with the highlights. It might mention average temperatures, flight prices and top attractions. If the reply is too long or too short, look for a button like “Summarise” or “Give me the key points” near the top of the reply.
You’ll know it worked when you see a neat paragraph that lists the main differences in simple language.

💬 Example:
Here’s a quick summary: Sydney offers warm beach days and iconic sights like the Opera House, while Melbourne shines with cooler weather, great coffee and artsy laneways.

---

## Step 4 — Ask for a deeper breakdown
Below the summary, type a follow-up question to get more detail. You can ask for costs, best areas to stay or even local food tips. If the chat box disappears, tap the bottom of the screen to bring it back.
The AI will add a new section with more facts and numbers.
You’ll know it worked when you see a new heading like “Costs” or “Neighbourhoods” appear in the chat.

💬 Example:
Can you give me a rough daily budget for each city, including food, transport and one paid attraction?

---

## Step 5 — Request a simple table for quick scanning
Ask the AI to turn the key facts into a table. Tables are easier to scan than long paragraphs. If the AI doesn’t make a table right away, type “Can you put that in a table?” or look for a button like “Format as table.”
You’ll see a clean table appear with columns for each city and rows for weather, cost and highlights.
You’ll know it worked when you see a neatly formatted table with two columns and several rows.

💬 Example:
Put the weather, cost and top attraction into a simple table so I can see it at a glance.

---

## Step 6 — Save or share the comparison
To keep the chat for later, look for a button like “Save chat” or “Copy link” near the top of the screen. If you want to share it with a friend, tap “Share” and choose how to send it. On a phone, you might need to tap the three dots (⋯) first.
You’ll know it worked when you see a confirmation message like “Chat saved” or when you can paste a link into a message.

💬 Example:
Tap the three dots in the top-right corner and choose “Copy link” to share the chat with your travel buddy.

---

## Common mistakes
- **Mistake:** Typing vague city names like “Gold Coast” instead of “Surfers Paradise.”
  **Fix:** Be specific so the AI doesn’t guess wrong. Try “Surfers Paradise vs Byron Bay” instead.

- **Mistake:** Expecting real-time prices or exact weather forecasts.
  **Fix:** Qwen Chat gives general guidance, not live data. Use it to narrow your choices, then check official sites for exact prices.

- **Mistake:** Skipping the follow-up question and missing key details.
  **Fix:** Always ask one extra question like “What’s the cheapest way to get between these two cities?” to get more useful info.

---

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Next time you’re torn between two holiday spots, open Qwen Chat and ask for a quick comparison. You’ll get the key facts without digging through dozens of travel blogs.

- **For your business or work:** If you plan team off-sites or client trips, use Qwen Chat to compare cities on cost, transport links and local amenities before booking anything.

- **If you're just getting started:** Start with two nearby cities you already know a little about. That way you can spot any mistakes in the AI’s answer and learn how to phrase better prompts.

---

## Try it now
Open [qwen.chat](https://qwen.chat) in your browser, type “Compare Melbourne and Brisbane for a 4-day winter holiday, focusing on weather, cost and things to do,” and hit send. In under a minute you’ll have a clear comparison to help you decide.
